question: Eric plans to compete in a triathlon. He can average \(2\) miles per hour in the \(\tfrac14\)-mile swim and \(6\) miles per hour in the \(3\)-mile run. His goal is to finish the triathlon in \(2\) hours. To accomplish his goal what must his average speed, in miles per hour, be for the \(15\)-mile bicycle ride?
solution:
Find the swimming and running times first, because the times for the three successive events add to \(2\) hours. Time equals distance divided by average speed, so swimming takes
\[
\frac{1/4}{2}=\frac18\text{ hour},
\]
and running takes \(\frac36=\frac12\) hour. This leaves
\[
2-\frac18-\frac12=\frac{11}{8}\text{ hours}
\]
for the bicycle ride. This is positive, so the required average speed over \(15\) miles is
\[
15\div\frac{11}{8}
=15\cdot\frac8{11}
=\frac{120}{11}\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{120}{11}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
